passage: The federal minimum wage should be raised significantly to ensure all workers can afford a basic standard of living. Currently, the federal minimum of $7.25 per hour is woefully inadequate—it hasn’t been increased since 2009, while the cost of housing, healthcare, and essentials has skyrocketed. A higher wage floor would reduce poverty, decrease reliance on public assistance, and stimulate economic growth by putting more money in the hands of low-income workers who spend it immediately in their communities. Opponents argue that raising wages could lead to job losses, but research on state-level increases shows minimal employment effects while significantly improving workers' well-being. My values prioritize economic justice and dignity for all workers; no one who works full-time should struggle to afford food or shelter. A higher minimum wage is also a matter of racial and gender equity, as women and people of color are disproportionately represented in low-wage jobs. While businesses may need time to adjust, the long-term benefits—reduced inequality, stronger consumer demand, and a fairer economy—far outweigh the costs. The government must act to ensure wages keep pace with the real cost of living.
